item.title: On the Luxemburg Functional in the Concave Regime with an Application to Nonlocal Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $p:[0,1]\to(0,1)$ a continuous function, we consider the Luxemburg functional \[ \Lambda_{p(\cdot)}(u):=\inf\left\{\delta>0:\int_0^1\left|\frac{u(t)}{\delta}\right|^{p(t)}\,dt\leq 1\right\}. \] We develop a suitable functional analytic framework for $\Lambda_{p(\cdot)}$ so that it can be incorporated into a positive order cone, which can then be used in the analysis of nonlocal differential equations having the general form \[ -A\left(\int_0^1 b(1-s)(u(s))^{p(s)}\,ds\right)u''(t) =\lambda f(t,u(t)),\qquad t\in(0,1). \] By means of a specific numerical example, we demonstrate that, as opposed to a methodology relying only on the supremum norm, our methodology via the Luxemburg functional yields an appreciably sharper localisation of any solutions of the nonlocal equation.
item.dc:creator: Christopher S. Goodrich, Gabriel Nakhl

item.title: Simultaneous Recovery of Wave Speeds and Initial Sources on Graphs via Redundant Frontier Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.36106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the simultaneous recovery of an unknown initial signal and unknown vertex wave speeds for the wave equation on a finite graph from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we first show that a single experiment determines both quantities under a new two-witness zero forcing condition and generic nondegeneracy assumptions. We then develop a more general frontier-propagation framework in which the redundancy required for simultaneous recovery is distributed across successive graph contours rather than localized at individual forcing vertices. We derive Lipschitz stability estimates for the frontier propagation problem. We also show the recovery and stability results extend to positively weighted graphs.
item.dc:creator: Amir Moradifam, Oliver P. Waite

item.title: Uniqueness and large-time continuous dependence in a doubly degenerate nutrient taxis system
item.description:
arXiv:2610.36117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: \[ u_t = 
abla \cdot (uv
abla u) - \chi 
abla\cdot (u^2 v
abla v) + \ell uv, \qquad \qquad v_t = \Delta v - uv, \] is considered in a smoothly bounded domain $\Omega\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ and with $\chi\ge 0$ and $\ell\ge 0$. Within a suitable concept of solvability, a statement on uniqueness of solutions emanating from initial data $(u_0,v_0)$ is derived under the mere assumption that $u_0\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ and $v_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ are such that $u_0\ge 0$ and $v_0>0$ in $\overline{\Omega}$; in particular, no condition on continuity of $u_0$ is imposed. This result is thereafter used to reveal that in physcally meaningful scenarios, for any initial data which are additionally assumed to be continuous and nontrivial, such solutions can always be found, and that these solutions depend continuously on the initial distributions not only in bounded sets of the form $\Omega	imes (0,T)$, but actually throughout $\Omega	imes (0,\infty)$, in a suitable sense.
item.dc:creator: Michael Winkler

item.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.36240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - V\beta$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.
item.dc:creator: David Gontier, Hanne Van Den Bosch

item.title: The Calder\'on problem for the fractional Schr\"odinger equation at a single point
item.description: arXiv:2610.36253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Calder\'on problem for the fractional Schr\"odinger equation and prove that the potential is determined by Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps at a single exterior point, with exterior inputs varying in a disjoint open set. This holds for continuous potentials for all $0<s<1$ and for bounded potentials when $s\geq 1/4$. For ordered nonnegative bounded potentials, one fixed nonzero nonnegative input and one point measurement suffice for every $0<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Harrach, Yi-Hsuan Lin

item.title: A fractional modular Poincar\'e--Wirtinger-type inequality in Sobolev spaces with variable exponents
item.description: arXiv:2610.36293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $p:\Omega\to[1,\infty)$ be a measurable, essentially bounded exponent; no regularity of $p$ -- in particular, no log-H\"older continuity -- is assumed. For a general non-negative measurable kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)$ admitting a radial bounding function $\kappa(x,r)$ in the second variable, we establish the fractional modular Poincar\'e--Wirtinger-type inequality $$ \iint_{\Omega\times\Omega}\mathcal{K}(x,y)\,|u(x)-u(y)|^{p(x)} d y\, d x \leqslant C\int_\Omega c(x)\left(\int_\Omega \frac{|\nabla u(z)|^{p(x)}}{|z-x|^{n-1+\theta}}\, d z\right) d x, $$ valid for every $u\in W^{1,1}(\Omega)$, in particular every $u\in W^{1,p(\cdot)}(\Omega)$, and every $\theta\in[0,1)$. Here $$ c(x)=\int_0^{D}r^{n+p(x)-2+\theta}\kappa(x,r)\,d r, $$ $D$ is the diameter of any fixed ball containing $\overline\Omega$, and the constant $C$ depends only on $n,p^+,\theta$ and the fixed domain $\Omega$. For the fractional kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)=|x-y|^{-n-\lambda p(x)}$ we obtain a variable-exponent Gagliardo-modular estimate. The proof replaces the starshaped chain decompositions used there by a combination of a Morrey-type estimate on starshaped domains, a positive-kernel proof of weighted Poincar\'e inequalities, and one reflection extension for the weights $|z-x|^{-(n-1+\theta)}$. The constants are uniform down to exponent $1$, and the inequalities are understood in the extended nonnegative sense when either side is infinite.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Di Fratta, Alberto Fiorenza, Leon Happ

item.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.36403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schr\"odinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.
item.dc:creator: David Damanik (Rice University), Long Li (Texas A&M University), Nicolae Strungaru (MacEwan University)

item.title: A self-contained proof of the variational characterization of the principal eigenvalue of $-\Delta+q$ under general Robin boundary conditions of non-classical type
item.description: arXiv:2610.36457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we are going to deliver a completely self-contained proof of the variational characterization of the principal eigenvalue of $-\Delta +q$ in $\Omega$ under Robin boundary conditions of non-classical type, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}+\beta(x)u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $\beta(x)$ is allowed to change sign on $\partial\Omega$. The classical case occurs in the very special case when $\beta\geq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$.
item.dc:creator: Juli\'an L\'opez-G\'omez, Alejandro Sahuquillo

item.title: Large data global strong solutions to the quantum Navier-Stokes equations with degenerate viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2610.36480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work is devoted to study the Cauchy problem for the quantum Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^N$, $N=2,3$, with density dependent viscosities $\mu(\rho)=\rho,\lambda(\rho)=0$, quantum capillarity $\kappa(\rho)=1/\rho$, which was derived by Dunn and Serrin (see Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 88(2):95-133, 1985) as a phase transition model. For arbitrarily large initial data satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions, with density positive at every finite point and vanishing at infinity, we prove the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without symmetry assumptions. The admissible pressure range is $\gamma\ge 1$ in two dimensions and $1\le\gamma< 8/3$ in three dimensions. On every finite time interval, the density remains pointwise comparable to its initial profile, and both the effective velocity and the logarithmic density gradient remain bounded. The central estimates require no uniform positive lower bound for the density. When $\gamma>1$, a suitable combination of the density and effective velocity equations allows the maximum principle to yield an $L^\infty$ bound for the effective velocity using only an upper bound for the density. We then introduce the relative density with respect to a fixed profile determined by the initial data. In the isothermal case $\gamma=1$, we combine estimates for this relative density with a scalar inequality involving the effective velocity and the logarithmic density to close the coupled estimates and obtain the effective velocity bound. Combining the relative-density bounds with weighted gradient estimates and localized De Giorgi iteration, we control the logarithmic density gradient and close the higher-order estimates.
item.dc:creator: Yongteng Gu, Xiangdi Huang, Muxi Lei

item.title: Global Well-posedness and Asymptotic Extinction for Keller-Segel Systems with Superlinear Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.36485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that solutions to deterministic Keller--Segel chemotaxis systems can blow up in finite time under certain conditions. To investigate whether noise can prevent such blow-up, we study parabolic--elliptic and fully parabolic Keller--Segel systems on smooth bounded domains with pointwise superlinear multiplicative It\^o noise $\sigma_0u^r\,\mathrm dW_t$, where $W$ is a real Brownian motion. Our results show that superlinear multiplicative noise can prevent finite-time blow-up in Keller--Segel systems. For $r>3/2$, we prove global existence and pathwise uniqueness of nonnegative mild solutions in arbitrary spatial dimension, for every $\sigma_0>0$. At $r=3/2$, both systems are globally well-posed in two dimensions for every positive noise intensity; in arbitrary dimension, the parabolic--elliptic system is global under $\sigma_0^2\ge2\chi$. For $r>3/2$ in the fully parabolic case, the proof combines a logarithmic estimate for the time derivative of the chemical signal with comparison of the local solution to the solution of a scalar stochastic differential equation. The two-dimensional case follows from mass quadratic variation, deterministic maximal regularity, and localized energy estimates. We also establish almost-sure $L^1$ extinction and algebraic decay of fractional mass moments.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Chen, Tusheng Zhang

item.title: On Solutions for Singular Toda System on Surfaces with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.36548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a singular Toda system with linear source terms on a compact surface $\Sigma$ with boundary $\partial\Sigma$. The aim is twofold. First, using isothermal coordinates and reflection arguments near the boundary, we perform blow-up analysis obtaining a compactness result. Second, by assuming that $\partial\Sigma$ has at least two connected components, we prove a general existence result via a min-max scheme combined with a retraction argument.
item.dc:creator: Zhengni Hu, Aleks Jevnikar, Sang-Hyuck Moon

item.title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{\alpha,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{\beta,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $\alpha+\beta>1$ and $\beta$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $\alpha p>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $\beta>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $\beta>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
item.dc:creator: Hanyu Teng

item.title: Time-Periodic Chemotaxis in Shifting Environments: Propagation and Planar Forced Waves in $\R^N$
item.description: arXiv:2610.36627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study time-periodic Keller--Segel dynamics in a translating KPP environment. In the parabolic--elliptic regime, we prove global boundedness, identify the sharp speed \(c_*=2\sqrt{\bar a\,\bar r}\), establish persistence in the interior region \(|s|<c_*\), \(s\cdot e<c\), and derive the complementary sharp upper bounds; for a moving favorable slab, the sign of a principal Floquet exponent determines persistence or extinction under the stated weighted-resolvent condition. For every fixed \(\tau\ge0\), under constant population diffusivity and sufficiently weak taxis, we further construct locally unique planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\). The main new analytic mechanisms are an exact Yukawa first-contact estimate, which controls the chemotactic drift at the KPP leading-edge scale without losing the sharp propagation threshold, and a two-sided weighted Fredholm--monodromy continuation framework for the temporally nonlocal signal equation, with explicit control of the far-field spectral gaps and the translational neutral mode. To the best of the author's knowledge, planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\) for shifting Keller--Segel systems have not been investigated in any previous studies; earlier forced-wave results are confined to substantially more restrictive settings, in particular one-dimensional parabolic--elliptic models. Thus the present construction provides the first multidimensional planar forced-wave theory for a time-periodic shifting Keller--Segel system with temporal signal memory.
item.dc:creator: Hoang-Hung Vo

item.title: Fluid Problems Posed on Closed Hypersurfaces: Circumventing the Saddle-Point Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.36641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a $d$-dimensional closed hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, we reformulate the (stationary) tangent Stokes, transient tangent Stokes, and transient tangent Navier-Stokes equations by replacing the divergence equation with a pressure Poisson equation, thereby circumventing their saddle-point structure. The pressure Poisson equation hinges on a commutator identity between the divergence and the surface diffusion operator, whose lower-order term depends on the Ricci curvature, and requires no boundary conditions for the pressure. We show that the reformulated operator is the composition of a linear, block-triangular data map with the primal operator. Consequently, each reformulation is well-posed if and only if the primal problem is, and solving it with arbitrary data amounts to solving the primal problem with a modified divergence datum. For hypersurfaces of class $C^2$ and data of the pressure Poisson equation in $H^{-1}$, the tangent Stokes reformulations can be posed in $H^1$-based spaces, which paves the way for conforming discretizations that do not require a discrete inf-sup condition.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo H. Nochetto, Mansur Shakipov

item.title: Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in $H^{1/2}_\bullet$
item.description: arXiv:2610.36676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation on the real line $\R$ in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). This regularity threshold for global well-posedness is optimal, as we show by constructing examples of ill-posedness in \(H^s_\bullet\) for any \(s<1/2\). Moreover, with the spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of initial data in the energy space, we prove that solutions in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\) asymptotically decouple as an infinite superposition of solitons. Our results extend the known global well-posedness and finite soliton resolution for rational data in \(H^\infty_\bullet\) to sharp global well-posedness and soliton resolution for general data in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). Different from rational solutions, general data can also involve an infinite discrete spectrum, which makes the reduction analysis framework on the finite rank no longer applicable. For sharp well-posedness, we present a new isometry criterion and stability results for resolvent transform in the explicit formula. For soliton resolution, we develop a spectral method for this equation based on direct resolvent analysis and a novel trace norm estimate that upgrades energy convergence to uniform convergence. Our argument also yields sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the generalized half-wave maps equation with targets in the complex Grassmannians, extending the classical sphere-valued case.
item.dc:creator: Fei Tang, Shou-Fu Tian

item.title: Dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations. For any $\gamma \in \left[ {0,\frac{1}{5}} \right)$, we establish the existence of $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder continuous weak solutions that exhibit a strict energy dissipation in expectation. For any $\gamma > \frac{1}{3}$, we prove that the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations do not possess dissipative solutions satisfying the corresponding spatial $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder regularity. It is well known that the stochastic forcing inevitably gives rise to additional stochastic effects to the Reynolds stresses, which cannot be treated by the differential estimates in the classical convex integration scheme introduced by Buckmaster, De Lellis, Isett and Sz\'{e}kelyhidi (Ann. Math., 182(1):127--172, 2015). To address this difficulty, we develop a novel material integration technique into the stochastic convex integration scheme, so that those stochastic Reynolds stresses are quantified.
item.dc:creator: Guanggan Chen, Wenhu Zhong

item.title: An inverse moving point source problem in inhomogeneous acoustic media: uniqueness, stability and reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.36830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed numerical method.
item.dc:creator: Dong Qiu, Xiang Xu, Yue Zhao

item.title: Principal profiles, characteristic communication and critical asymptotics for cooperative nonlocal systems on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2610.36851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study cooperative nonlocal transport on a circle with species-dependent constant velocities and arbitrary $L^1$ probability kernels. For periodic coefficients, the period map is a compact perturbation of the no-jump map. We construct separate receiving and sending characteristic scans: under a two-tree condition based at one active component, a positive Floquet profile exists exactly when the full period map has strictly larger spectral radius than its no-jump part. The other jump rates may vanish. The scans provide an integral minorant and positive jump return; a separate coefficient inequality verifies the spectral gap. Smooth locking examples distinguish communication from frozen-time mixing, while a resonant example separates positive return from spectral separation. Autonomous nonzero velocities and union-graph connectivity yield a simple principal pair; one active component suffices for exponential mixing. We also prove local perturbation results. For quadratic self-regulation, the same principal projection gives a transverse response whose averaged cubic coefficient is a nonnegative asymptotic variance. It determines both the critical $t^{-2}\log t$ correction and the second-order period-averaged amplitude of the positive branch.
item.dc:creator: Bing He

item.title: A class of degenerate elliptic problems involving the Grushin operator: critical mass and ground states
item.description: arXiv:2610.36927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the following degenerate elliptic equation with combined nonlinearities and prescribed mass \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \begin{cases} -\Delta_{\gamma}u+\omega u+|u|^{p-2}u=|u|^{q-2}u \ \ \mbox{in }\mathbb{R}^{N}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}} |u|^{2} \mathrm{d}z=c, \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $\Delta_{\gamma}$ is the Grushin operator and $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$ appears as an unknown Lagrange multiplier. We characterize the critical mass threshold and the energy ground state solutions. Firstly, we prove the existence of optimizers for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin operator together with estimates for the related best constant. Secondly, we characterize the critical mass by the best constant of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and prove the existence of $x$-radial energy ground state solutions. Finally, we describe the relation between the $x$-radial action and energy ground state solutions, and the optimizers of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. The strategy developed here is based on the interplay between the mass-preserving scaling and a sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. It therefore suggests possible extensions to other prescribed-mass problems with competing homogeneous terms and threshold-mass phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Aleks Jevnikar, Senli Liu, Yu Su

item.title: Emergence of large densities in a chemotaxis system with signal-dependent motility
item.dc:creator: Max Hegenbart

item.title: Extended stability timescales for the 2D3C rotating stratified Boussinesq equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the time evolution of a vertical-slice model for incompressible inhomogeneous rotating fluids perturbed around a stably stratified rest state with linear buoyancy profile. For $\varepsilon$-small localized initial data with vanishing potential vorticity, we prove that solutions remain of size $O(\varepsilon)$ up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-\frac43}$, and up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ in a regime where the Brunt--V\"ais\"al\"a frequency and the Coriolis parameter are comparable. The first result relies on linear dispersion with amplitude decay rate $\langle t\rangle^{-\frac12}$, while the second exploits the absence of three-wave resonances via a normal form transformation. Our results remain valid for small nonzero initial potential vorticity, whose size is propagated by means of an intrinsic change of coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Augusto Del Zotto, Luca Melzi, Haoling Xiang

item.title: Global well-posedness and scattering of energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} i\partial_t u + \Delta u = |u|^{\frac{4}{d-2}} u, u(0) = u_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} on hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d(d \geq 4)$. We mainly utilize the concentration-compactness/rigidity method. We establish a linear profile decomposition on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces and prove that the nonlinear profile on hyperbolic spaces can be approximated by the solutions of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on Euclidean spaces, then obtaining the global well-posedness and scattering of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the high-dimensional hyperbolic space.
item.dc:creator: Shunqin Zhang, Jiqiang Zheng, Yunrui Zheng

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Large Time Asymptotic Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Compressible Viscous Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.37078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem to the compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system in $\mathbb{R}^3$, in which the velocity is planar while the magnetic field is vertical. For regular initial data with small energy but possibly large oscillations, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solution with vacuum. In addition, the large-time behavior of the solution is investigated. A key ingredient is an application of the Bourgain--Brezis divergence estimate to handle the total pressure $\rho^\gamma+m^2$ for any adiabatic index $\gamma>1$. This enables us to control both components of the total pressure, $\rho^\gamma$ and $m^2$, by a single estimate that remains valid in the presence of vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, our result is the first one on global solvability to the compressible, viscous, non-resistive MHD system in the special 2$\frac12$-dimensional whole space allowing vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxu Li, Boqiang L\"u, Bing Yuan

item.title: Large-bulk-viscosity limit for two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluids with vacuum
item.description:
arXiv:2610.37099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid system on the torus $\mathbb T^2$. The initial density is bounded and nonnegative and may contain vacuum, while the initial velocity and microrotation belong to $H^1(\mathbb T^2)$. For sufficiently large bulk viscosity $
u$, we prove the global-in-time existence of solutions without a smallness assumption on the $H^1$ size of the data, provided that the initial compressible component is well prepared in the sense that $\sqrt{
u}\|\operatorname{div}u_0\|_{L^2}$ is uniformly bounded. The proof combines the effective viscous flux with a coupled energy scheme that exploits the vorticity--microrotation dissipation at both the basic and material-derivative levels. For the linear pressure law, we also prove uniqueness in the stated solution class by means of a coupled backward parabolic problem, logarithmic interpolation, and Osgood's lemma. For fixed initial data with $\operatorname{div}u_0=0$, we also justify the limit $
u	o\infty$: every sequence of the corresponding solutions admits a subsequence converging to a solution of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible micropolar system.
item.dc:creator: Zijian Du, Sen Yang, Xinglong You

item.title: Tumor growth models with nutrient consumption
item.description: arXiv:2610.37144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the saturation free boundary of the cell density and its interaction with the nutrient depletion interface in a coupled parabolic model for tumor growth with sublinear reactions. We establish a sharp quadratic--superquadratic growth dichotomy along the saturation interface and quantify the degeneration of quadratic profiles as they approach the joint saturation--depletion boundary. We further show that intrinsic regularity of the saturation interface can occur only at joint free boundary points, where half-space blow-ups of either component determine a unique joint blow-up profile. Finally, we prove a local backward coincidence between the joint and nutrient free boundaries near regular points, which yields spatial and temporal regularity of the joint interface.
item.dc:creator: Dami\~ao J. Ara\'ujo, Rafayel Teymurazyan, Jos\'e Miguel Urbano

item.title: Uniform parameter bounds for weighted exponential equations on simply connected domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.37177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider positive solutions of \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -\Delta u=p\lambda h(x)u^{p-1}\mathrm{e}^{u^p}&\text{in }\Omega,\\ u>0&\text{in }\Omega,\\ u=0&\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p\in[1,2]$, $\lambda>0$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded simply connected domain and $h\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ is positive on $\overline\Omega$. The cases $p=1$ and $p=2$ correspond to the Liouville and Moser-Trudinger equations, respectively. We prove that the normalized parameter \begin{equation*} \beta=\frac{\lambda p^2}{2}\left(\int_\Omega h(\mathrm{e}^{u^p}-1)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2-p}{p}}\left(\int_\Omega hu^p\mathrm{e}^{u^p}\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{p}} \end{equation*} is bounded by a constant depending only on $\Omega$ and $h$, uniformly over all $p\in[1,2]$, $\lambda>0$ and positive solutions. At $p=2$, this excludes positive constrained critical points of the weighted Moser-Trudinger functional at sufficiently large Dirichlet energies. For $p=2$ and $h\equiv1$, we further prove that the energy converges uniformly to $4\pi$ as $\lambda\to0$ when $\Omega$ is convex. We also develop a boundary exclusion argument for positive weights that rules out boundary blow-up for $1<p<2$ without a priori energy bound.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Ge Chen, Peng Luo, Shuangjie Peng, Fulin Zhong

item.title: Quantitative periodic homogenization and uniform regularity for nonlocal equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study quantitative homogenization for a class of nonlocal equations with periodically oscillating H\"older continuous coefficients. For Dirichlet problems in bounded $C^{1,\alpha}$ domains, we prove $L^2$ convergence rates that are expected to be optimal. In addition, we establish interior Lipschitz estimates and optimal boundary H\"older estimates for weak solutions, with constants independent of the period of oscillation.
item.dc:creator: Kyeongbae Kim, Simon Nowak, Marvin Weidner

item.title: The homogeneity function of the fractional $p$-Laplacian and optimal asymptotic exponents for critical Hardy-Sobolev equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $N \geq 2$, $s\in (0,1)$, and $p \in (1, \infty)$ with $N>sp$. For the fractional $p$-Laplacian, the power function $|x|^{-\gamma}$ with $0<\gamma<\frac{N}{p-1}$ satisfies $$(-\Delta_p)^s \big(|x|^{-\gamma}\big)=\Phi(\gamma)|x|^{-\gamma(p-1)-sp} \, \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}.$$ Starting from the power function formula of Del Pezzo and Quaas (2026), we derive a paired integral representation of $\Phi$, and show that $\Phi$ is strictly increasing and then strictly decreasing, with a unique maximum at $\frac{N-sp}{p}$. This maximum $\bar\mu:=\Phi(\frac{N-sp}{p})$ equals one half of the sharp fractional Hardy constant. Consequently, for every $0<\mu<\bar\mu$, the equation $\Phi(\gamma)=\mu$ has exactly two roots $0<\gamma_{-}(\mu)<\frac{N-sp}{p}<\gamma_{+}(\mu)<\frac{N-sp}{p-1}$. These roots determine the homogeneous solutions $|x|^{-\gamma_{-}(\mu)}$ and $|x|^{-\gamma_{+}(\mu)}$ of the Hardy equation \begin{equation*} (-\Delta_p)^s u - \mu \frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}}=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}, \; u> 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N \setminus \{0\}. \end{equation*} For $0<\mu<\bar\mu$, we then study the following critical Hardy-Sobolev equation \begin{align}\tag{$\mathcal{P}$}\label{P} (-\Delta_p)^s u-\mu \frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}} = u^{\frac{Np}{N-sp}-1} \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N, \; u > 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N. \end{align} Let $p \geq 2$ and $U$ be a positive, radially symmetric, nonincreasing finite-energy weak solution to \eqref{P}. We prove that there exists $C>0$ for which \begin{align*} U(x) \leq C|x|^{-\gamma_-(\mu)}\;\text{as }|x| \rightarrow 0,\quad \text{ and } \quad U(x)\le C|x|^{-\gamma_+(\mu)} \; \text{as }|x| \rightarrow \infty. \end{align*} Further, we show that $\gamma_-(\mu)$ and $\gamma_+(\mu)$ are the optimal exponents describing the singularity at the origin and the decay at infinity respectively.
item.dc:creator: Nirjan Biswas, Debangana Mukherjee

item.title: Global Existence and Scattering of a Class of Two-Dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.37220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a class of two-dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg systems of quantum hydrodynamic type, we establish global existence and scattering for small, smooth, spatially localized perturbations of a constant equilibrium with irrotational velocity. This extends the three-dimensional well-posedness result of Song [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 2157--2224] to two dimensions. Our proof follows the space-time resonance approach developed by Deng, Ionescu, Pausader, and Pusateri for the three-dimensional gravity-capillary water-wave system. The new ingredients are twofold. First, to allow non-neutral initial data, we exploit the absence of space resonances and of time resonances---including those arising after the second and third iterations---and the improved approximate-finite-speed-of-propagation bounds. Second, in the energy estimates, we adapt the almost orthogonality argument used in the works of Ionescu--Pausader and Guo--Ionescu--Pausader to the regime in which the input and output frequencies are all comparable to $1$. In this regime, time resonances may occur and the relevant curvature quantity may vanish.
item.dc:creator: Han Cui, Linhao Shi

item.title: A new approach to compactly supported stationary Euler flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.37251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth, compactly supported stationary Euler flows in two and three dimensions. The three-dimensional flows are axisymmetric with swirl, and their pressure varies along some streamlines. The planar flows are not locally radial. Both constructions start from simple radial profiles, which we perturb by solving scalar elliptic equations on fixed domains. We choose these equations so that their solutions can be exactly constant on open sets and meet these constant regions smoothly. Comparison arguments produce the constant regions, while an a priori regularity theorem ensures that all derivatives vanish where a solution meets them. This gives compact support and smoothness without having to describe the boundary of the support.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Enciso, Antonio J. Fern\'andez

item.title: Solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present paper is devoted to exhibit solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic. With ambiguous non-conservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. This jump condition is obtained from the information given by the travelling wave solutions of the viscous extension of the system that involves the diffusion terms arising from the physics of the problem. We are then able to determine the simple waves of the non-conservative system studied here and we are able to construct some solutions of the Riemann problem of interest.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Berthon (LMJL), Marie Compain (LMJL), Carlos Par\'es, Ernesto Pimentel-Garc\'ia

item.title: Regularity Effects on the Small-Diffusion Asymptotics of the Principal Eigenvalue: Non-convergence and Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.37259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior as \(d\to0^+\) of the principal eigenvalue \(\lambda(d)\) of the one-dimensional elliptic problem \[ \begin{cases} -d\phi''(x)-2\alpha m'(x)\phi'(x)+c(x)\phi(x) =\lambda(d)\phi(x), & x\in(a,b),\\ \phi'(a)=\phi'(b)=0, \end{cases} \] where \(\alpha>0\) is fixed, \(m\in C^{1,1}([a,b])\), and \(c\in C([a,b])\). We assume that \(m'=0\) only at \(x_0\in(a,b)\), where \(m\) attains a strict minimum. Within this class, we construct a counterexample $m\in C^{1,1}$ for which \(\lambda(d)\) has two distinct subsequential limits as \(d\to0^+\), leading to the non-convergence of $\lambda(d)$. We then consider another class of $C^{1,1}$ advection functions for which $m'(x)/(x-x_0)$ has positive one-sided limits at $x_0$. For this class, we prove that $\lambda(d)$ converges as $d\to0^+$. Thus, \(C^{1,1}\) regularity alone does not ensure convergence of the principal eigenvalue, even when \(m\) has exactly one strict interior critical minimal point.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Zhang

item.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
item.description: arXiv:2610.37401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Blessing Neam\c{t}u, Hongjun Gao, Haoyuan Li

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Sharp Poincar\'e inequality for $W_0^{2,p}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first eigenvalue of the $p$-bilaplacian over a domain $\Omega$ is the inverse of the Poincar\'e constant for $W_0^{2,p}(\Omega)$. In dimension two, we prove that it is minimised by disks under area constraint, thereby obtaining a sharp uniform Poincar\'e inequality.
item.dc:creator: Rom\'eo Leylekian

item.title: Sharp Planar Anisotropic Capillarity Outside Convex Obstacles and Two-Point Rigidity of Transported Boundary Images
item.description: arXiv:2610.37440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a convex surface tension $\varphi$ and the wall-energy density $\sigma(n)=-\lambda\,\varphi(-n)$, we prove sharp capillary inequalities outside arbitrary convex planar obstacles for $-1<\lambda\leq0$ and every finite-perimeter competitor of finite positive volume, including non-even and crystalline tensions. Equality holds precisely for translated dilates of Wulff caps in minimum-volume directions, with the entire truncating facet resting on a flat supporting face. A uniform quantitative estimate controls component concentration, shape up to translation, and directional cap-volume excess. The proof combines exact filling, planar completion, and quantitative Wulff stability. For the transport $D\Phi$, $\Phi=\varphi^2/2$, the zero-adhesion boundary-image estimate characterizes centered ellipsoids among even anisotropies with $\Phi\in C^3$ away from the origin and positive definite Hessian. Two-point slab tests with arbitrary boundary data suffice: their projection balances yield a cubic identity forcing $\Phi$ to be quadratic. Facets and smooth perturbations provide counterexamples to the transported estimate, including failures at prescribed adhesion levels in $(-1,1)$. Strict finite deficits persist under Hausdorff perturbations of the Wulff body. The classification concerns an unrestricted boundary-data property, stronger than the image estimate needed only for traces of auxiliary Neumann solutions.
item.dc:creator: Lisbeth Carrero, Alexander Quaas, Andres Zuniga

item.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Lojasiewicz Estimates for a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structure of degree $1$ minimisers of a Baby-Skyrme energy of maps $u:\Sigma \to S^2$ regularised by a Sacks-Uhlenbeck perturbation, and we establish quantitative convergence rates to a simple bubble tree consisting of a single degree $1$ bubble and a constant base map.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Global H\"{o}lder solvability for parabolic equations with interior Morrey data
item.description: arXiv:2610.37528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global H\"{o}lder solvability for uniformly parabolic divergence-form equations with locally finite measure data under an interior Morrey growth condition and a capacity density condition on the spatial domain. The parabolic distance to the initial and lateral boundary is assumed bounded on the source support. For nonnegative data, we establish necessity results that demonstrate the sharpness of the growth and domain assumptions. We also derive estimates for divergence forcing, prove solvability for equations with lower-order terms, and obtain convergence rates in periodic homogenization.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Local regularity for solutions to singular and degenerate quasilinear parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to prove local H\"{o}lder continuity for weak solutions to quasilinear parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type under finite integrability assumptions on the forcing, covering the supercritical singular range and the entire degenerate regime. The key ingredient is an $L^\infty$-valued temporal H\"{o}lder estimate of the solution after any fixed positive waiting time, which is achieved by coupling a time-rescaling argument with De Giorgi iteration. We also provide counterexamples involving forcing terms with weaker spatial integrability to show that even bounded continuous solutions with compatible data may possess no positive temporal H\"{o}lder exponent. In particular, these examples establish the sharpness of the spatial integrability threshold in the degenerate case. Finally, a separate counterexample is constructed to demonstrate that the temporal Lipschitz endpoint can fail for bounded continuous forcing when it depends on time.
item.dc:creator: Yan Li, Zhiwen Zhao

item.title: Boundary Plateau Laws I
item.description: arXiv:2610.37559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis, Federico Glaudo

item.title: Boundary Plateau Laws II
item.description: arXiv:2610.37560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis, Federico Glaudo

item.title: Diffusive-dispersive traveling waves and kinetic relations. Generic flux with multiple inflection points
item.description: arXiv:2610.37623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the broad class of scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with generic non-convex fluxes, which may thus have an arbitrary finite number of inflection points. We investigate the properties of classical and nonclassical shock waves realized as traveling-wave limits of a linear diffusive-dispersive regularization and provide a phase-plane classification beyond the case of a single inflection point. Within the speed range of the generalized Maxwell construction, our main result classifies the left outgoing profiles by their limiting equilibria. In an elementary bowtie configuration, we prove the existence of nonclassical shock profiles with arbitrarily many oscillations. For nested configurations, we order the saddle connections on each entry interval, taking account of inaccessible saddles. We show that the number of oscillations present in the non-classical shock depends on the diffusion-dispersion ratio, and tends to infinity along the elementary families of saddle connections as this ratio tends to zero. Our construction is based on a generalization of Maxwell's equal area rule, which provides us with an invariant region in the phase space for the study of diffusive-dispersive traveling waves.
item.dc:creator: Marc Laforest, Philippe G. LeFloch

item.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct two distinct solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation with the same initial vorticity in $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$. The vorticities are compactly supported in space and have mean zero, so the corresponding velocities have finite energy. The nonuniqueness mechanism is a cascade of transitions in quadrupole dynamics across infinitely many scales.
item.dc:creator: Hyungjun Choi

item.title: Optimization of the second Robin eigenvalue on a planar exterior domain under fixed area constraint
item.description: arXiv:2610.34320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Robin Laplacian on a planar exterior domain with a negative boundary parameter. For a negative boundary parameter of a sufficiently large absolute value this operator has at least two negative eigenvalues below the bottom of the essential spectrum. We prove that under a fixed area constraint and convexity assumption on the bounded complement of the exterior domain the second Robin eigenvalue is maximized by the exterior of the disk. The inequality is strict for every exterior of a non-circular domain whenever the comparison disk has a negative second eigenvalue. The proof modifies the parallel-coordinate method by allowing the angular phase of a trial function to vary with the distance from the boundary. This result resolves the first item in a 2024 conjecture by the authors under an additional convexity assumption. Relaxing the convexity and the perimeter constraint remain open problems.
item.dc:creator: David Krejcirik, Vladimir Lotoreichik

item.title: A Counterexample to a Bourgain-Brezis Sum-Space Estimate
item.description: arXiv:2610.35882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A question of Bourgain and Brezis, later restated as Open Problem 7.1 by Brezis, asks whether the $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ norm of a mean-zero scalar function is controlled by the ambient $H^{-1/2}+L^1$ sum norm of its gradient. We show that this estimate fails in every dimension $N\geq 2$. More precisely, for every integer $K\geq 16$, we construct a smooth real-valued mean-zero function $\Phi_K$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ such that $|\nabla\Phi_K|{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}\leq C$ and $|\Phi_K|{H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)}\geq cK^{1/4}-C$, where the absolute constants $c,C>0$ are independent of $N$ and $K$. Equivalently, the ratio of the gradient-constrained decomposition cost to the ambient decomposition cost is unbounded. The construction applies the Hodge projection to a smooth approximation of a normal vector measure on a codimension-one sheet. Its potential records lacunary partial sums at geometrically separated distances from the sheet. A scale-path lower bound, combined with an odd critical Hardy inequality, excludes uniformly bounded $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ decompositions.
item.dc:creator: Chenye Zhang (Peking University)

item.title: Accelerating Langevin Dynamics with Weighted Laplacian Flow: Global Well-Posedness and Exponential Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.35892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study an accelerated Langevin equation in which the classical overdamped Langevin drift is supplemented by a nonlocal gradient velocity determined through a target-weighted Poisson equation. The target $p$ is only assumed to be strictly positive and need not be normalized. Writing the dynamics in terms of $\omega=\log(p/q)$ yields a coupled parabolic-elliptic system whose parabolic component contains the usual Langevin diffusion, whereas the elliptic component generates a global transport. The system is invariant under multiplication of $p$ by a positive constant. On a bounded smooth domain with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, we establish global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for strictly positive $C^{2+\alpha}$ target weights and compatible $C^{2+\alpha}$ initial data. For long-time behavior, the oscillation of $\omega$ decays at the explicit rate $e^{-t}$ and the solution density exponentially converges to target density. Moreover, an exact entropy-dissipation identity holds relative to the target density, in which the relative Fisher information and the Jeffreys divergence give the two dissipation mechanisms associated with the Langevin and weighted-Poisson components. In particular, KL divergence also converges to zero with rate $e^{-t}$ without a convexity assumption on the target.
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Cai, Weiye Gan, Borui Miao, Zuoqiang Shi

item.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.36125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $\Delta_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Dias

item.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
item.description: arXiv:2610.36242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.
item.dc:creator: Robin Ming Chen, Kristoffer Varholm, Annie Grace Wang

item.title: The inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on klt Fano varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.36414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a K\"ahler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Tam\'as Darvas, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
item.description: arXiv:2610.36741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kozyrev

item.title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high odd dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a recent paper~\cite{BGW}, Bizo\'n, Glogi\'c, and Wasserman (BGW) reduced the classification of smooth self-similar Yang--Mills profiles in odd spatial dimensions $d\ge11$ to an algebraic problem of counting roots of an explicit polynomial in a prescribed interval. Two roots correspond to explicit profiles. BGW conjectured that there is exactly one additional root and verified this in a range of odd dimensions. Here, we prove the existence of an additional root, and hence of a third smooth self-similar profile, in every odd dimension $d\geq11$. The proof combines an endpoint sign calculation for the resonance polynomial with an algebraic argument showing that the third root is distinct from the two explicit ones. Uniqueness remains open in general.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Bizo\'n, Robert Kluszczy\'nski

item.title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
item.description: arXiv:2610.36815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Chen, Armen Shirikyan, Shengquan Xiang

item.title: A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.37453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\sigma(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=\sigma(x_1)\sigma(x_3)-\sigma(x_2)\sigma(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We show that $\mathscr{M}$ is a complete embedded minimal hypersurface with infinitely many isolated singularities, which are exactly the vertices of the regular honeycomb of $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ by $24$-cells. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $\pi/2$ at each singularity. The isometry group of $\mathscr{M}$ is generated by the translations of the root lattice $D_4$ and a hyperoctahedral group of order $384$ fixing the centre of a $24$-cell; it has index three in the symmetry group of the honeycomb, acts transitively on the singular points, and contains a symmetry which is not visible from the defining equation. Seen from the centre of a $24$-cell, $\mathscr{M}$ is the zero set of a theta series of a translate of the Hurwitz quaternions, which makes the whole symmetry group manifest; the sections of $\mathscr{M}$ by a family of parallel hyperplanes are triply periodic surfaces with cubic symmetry which change topology through conical points. Finally, $\mathscr{M}$ is obtained from a union of $2$-planes by attaching cones over $2$-tori, and its quotient by the lattice of periods is a compact minimal hypersurface in a flat $4$-torus with exactly three singular points and infinite Morse index; we show that its regular part is one-sided and compute its Euler characteristic and integral homology.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir G. Tkachev

item.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.
item.dc:creator: Alex Cohen, Zhenhao Li, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.
item.dc:creator: E. Petrov, R. Salimov, R. Taranets

item.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincar\'e Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.37659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincar\'e inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Letrouit, Tudor Manole

item.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2111.05822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.
item.dc:creator: Anis Dhifaoui

item.title: Topological Anderson Insulators by homogenization theory
item.description: arXiv:2311.15678v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central property of (Chern) topological insulators is the presence of robust asymmetric transport along interfaces separating two-dimensional insulating materials in different topological phases. A Topological Anderson Insulator is an insulator whose topological phase is induced by spatial fluctuations. This paper proposes a mathematical model of perturbed Dirac equations and shows that for sufficiently large and highly oscillatory perturbations, the systems is in a different topological phase than the unperturbed model. In particular, a robust asymmetric transport indeed appears at an interface separating perturbed and unperturbed phases. The theoretical results are based on careful estimates of resolvent operators in the homogenization theory of Dirac equations and on the characterization of topological phases by the index of an appropriate Fredholm operator.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Bal, Thuyen Dang

item.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels in Double Conic Domains
item.description: arXiv:2411.15793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the even and odd Jacobi heat kernels defined in the context of the multidimensional double cone and its surface, the multidimensional hyperboloid and its surface, and the multidimensional paraboloid and its surface. By integrating the framework of Jacobi polynomials on these domains, as analyzed by Xu, with contemporary methods developed by Nowak, Sj\"ogren, and Szarek for obtaining sharp estimates of the spherical heat kernel, we establish genuinely sharp estimates for the even and odd Jacobi heat kernel in the double conic settings, and for the even Jacobi heat kernel on hyperbolic settings. We also discuss the limitations encountered in extending these results to the remaining settings.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Hanrahan

item.title: Phase separation in multiply periodic materials with fine microstructures
item.description: arXiv:2506.14462v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Cahn-Hilliard model for phase separation in composite materials with multiple periodic microstructures. These are modeled by considering a highly oscillating potential. The focus of this paper is in the case where the scales of the microstructures are smaller than that of phase separation. We provide a compactness result and prove that the {\Gamma}-limit of the energy is a multiple of the perimeter. In particular, using the recently introduced unfolding operator for multiple scales, we show that the taking the limit of all of the scales together is equivalent to taking one limit at the time, starting from the smaller scale and keeping the larger fixed.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Cristoferi, Luca Pignatelli

item.title: Free boundary regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem
item.description: arXiv:2506.18741v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem. Assuming only that the initial temperature is integrable, we prove that the free boundary, known to have jump discontinuities as a function of the time variable, is $C^1$ as a function of the space variable, and is $C^{\infty}$ outside of a closed, countable set, which we describe explicitly. We also prove that, as conjectured in arXiv:1902.05174, the set of positive times when a jump occurs cannot have accumulation points. In addition, we prove that short-time uniqueness of physical solutions implies global uniqueness, which allows us to obtain uniqueness for very general initial data that fall outside the scope of the current well-posedness regime. In particular, we answer two questions left open in arXiv:1811.12356, arXiv:2302.13097, regarding the global uniqueness of solutions. We proceed by deriving a weighted obstacle problem satisfied by the solutions, which we exploit to establish regularity and non-degeneracy estimates and to classify the free boundary points. We also establish a backward propagation of oscillation property, which allows us to control the occurrence of future jumps in terms of the past oscillation of the solution.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Munoz

item.title: Shape differentials and sensitivity of the heat equation
item.description: arXiv:2506.21196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider Dirichlet and Neumann problems for the heat equation in a domain containing an interior hole. The domain has a fixed outer boundary and a variable inner boundary determined by a diffeomorphism $\phi$. We analyze the maps that assign to the infinite-dimensional shape parameter $\phi$ the corresponding solutions, and we prove that they are smooth. Motivated by applications to inverse problems, we then compute the differentials with respect to $\phi$ of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann and Neumann-to-Dirichlet maps.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Dalla Riva, Paolo Luzzini, Paolo Musolino

item.title: Nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on noncompact quantum graphs
item.description: arXiv:2510.20658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on finite noncompact metric graphs with Kirchhoff-type conditions. For a nondecreasing nonlinearity of arbitrary finite superquadratic growth, a sufficiently long pendant path guarantees ground states whose nonrelativistic limits are Schr\"odinger ground states. Every choice of these states is relatively compact in $H^1$ and satisfies a uniform exponential decay estimate. On general graphs, we prove a compactness alternative: loss of compactness requires at least the action of a full-line ground state. Translated line profiles show that the loss constants are sharp. The proof combines an $H^1$ estimate in terms of the action with convergence of Dirac fiber maxima to Schr\"odinger ray maxima. For power nonlinearities, we give an integral criterion in terms of the dimensionless pendant length and obtain the same conclusions for arbitrary edge lengths on four graph topologies.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Michael Ruzhansky, Guoyan Wei, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Inverse stability for hyperbolic equations with different initial conditions
item.description: arXiv:2511.01688v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish Lipschitz stability for both the potential and the initial conditions from a single boundary measurement in the context of a hyperbolic boundary initial value problem. In our setting, the initial conditions are allowed to differ for different potentials. Compared to the traditional B-K method, our approach does not require the time reflection step. This advantage opens a route towards applying our method to the fixed angle inverse scattering problem, which remains unresolved for the single incident wave case. To achieve our result, we impose a pointwise comparison estimate on the Laplacian of the differences of the initial conditions, together with a positivity condition on one of the initial positions. The assumption generalizes previous stability results that usually assume the difference to be zero. We propose the initial-potential problem and establish a Lipschitz stability, then propose an iterative reconstruction scheme and show its geometric convergence. The initial-potential problem serves as an attempt to relate initial boundary value problem to the scattering problem, and to explore the possibility of relaxing the positivity requirement on the initial data. We also establish a new pointwise Carleman estimate, whose proof is significantly shorter and the reasoning is much clearer than existing proofs.
item.dc:creator: Shiqi Ma

item.title: Generic small-scale creation in the two-dimensional Euler equation
item.description: arXiv:2603.13079v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is globally well-posed for smooth initial data. We prove that, for all $p>2$ and for a dense $G_\delta$ set of initial vorticities in $W^{1,p}$, the solutions lose regularity in infinite time, in the sense that the $L^p$ norm of the gradient of the vorticity is unbounded. This confirms a long-standing conjecture of Yudovich.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Alazard, Ayman Rimah Said

item.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
item.description: arXiv:2604.20469v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Morgulis, Karrar Malal

item.title: Volumetric density estimates for nonlocal minimal surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.02176v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we prove that viscosity subsolutions to nonlocal mean curvature-type equations satisfy universal volumetric estimates at all scales provided their boundary has zero Lebesgue measure. Our results hold for a general class of symmetric kernels including kernels that are comparable to the fractional Laplacian. Furthermore, we prove that subsolutions with low density (with respect to a universal constant) necessarily have `fat boundary', that is, have topological boundary with positive Lebesgue measure.
item.dc:creator: Mateusz Kwa\'snicki, Jack Thompson

item.title: A Sharp Regularity Threshold for Uniqueness in Riemannian Calder\'on-type Problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.21705v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp regularity threshold for uniqueness in two anisotropic Calder\'on-type inverse problems in dimension $n\ge 3$. The main setting is the Riemannian Schr\"odinger problem with fixed scalar potential: for a prescribed nonconstant analytic function $V$, we study whether the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $-\Delta_g+V$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ determines the unknown metric $g$. The natural gauge is the group of boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms preserving $V$. We show that, while analytic metrics are uniquely determined modulo this gauge by a minor adaptation of the Lassas--Uhlmann reconstruction theorem, uniqueness fails densely in every non-analytic Gevrey class $G^\sigma$, $\sigma>1$. In fact, our counterexamples are not isometric in the sense that they are not connected by the pushforward of any diffeomorphism of $\overline\Omega$. We also prove the analogous sharp threshold for the anisotropic Calder\'on problem at fixed nonzero frequency, thereby upgrading the previously known finite-regularity counterexamples to Gevrey and $C^\infty$ regularity. The two constructions use different scalar mechanisms: for fixed potentials, the nonconstant potential itself provides a local coordinate, while at nonzero frequency one uses a compactly supported prescribed-Jacobian lemma in Gevrey spaces. Thus analyticity is the exact threshold for uniqueness in both problems.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Daud\'e, Alberto Enciso, Bernard Helffer, Niky Kamran, Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau

item.title: Uniqueness of the blow-up for some Alt-Phillips cones
item.description: arXiv:2606.17015v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish uniqueness of blow-ups, with sharp quantitative convergence, for several classes of singular minimizing cones in the Alt-Phillips problem, in the range $\gamma\in(0,2)$. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness at every free boundary point in dimensions $d=2,3,4$ for $\gamma\in(1,2)$, and in dimensions $d\geq 5$ for $\gamma\in\left(1,\frac32\right)$. The proof of uniqueness is based on three new logarithmic epiperimetric inequalities. The sharp distinction between polynomial and logarithmic convergence is governed by a finite-dimensional integrability condition (sub-integrability) for the spherical linearized problem. We prove this sharpness for the radial cone and its cylindrical extensions through an explicit integrability and bifurcation analysis, showing in particular that logarithmic convergence may be sharp even in dimension two. In contrast, we show that the one-dimensional cone is exceptional: although the integrability condition fails, the convergence is polynomial. Finally, we characterize the minimality of the radial cone in terms of $d$ and $\gamma$ by means of a one-dimensional calibration argument, exhibiting in dimension $d\geq6$ a nontrivial regime in which the radial cone is stable but not minimizing.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Carducci, Giorgio Tortone

item.title: Elliptic Superlevel Sets in the Class $\OO_C$: Boundary-Layer Geometry and Stability of the Return Map
item.description: arXiv:2607.16912v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $\Omega \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-\Delta u = f$ in $\Omega$ ($u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $\Omega_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$. We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partial\Omega_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partial\Omega_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)\nu(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality.
