Using normal-graph formulas, we show $\Omega_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$. The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed El Morsalani, Mohammd Barkatou

item.title: Finite-time blow-up for the real-valued defocusing energy-supercritical NLW
item.description: arXiv:2610.06678v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct real-valued solutions of the defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equation $\partial_t^2u-\Delta u+u^p=0$ that blow up in finite time from smooth, compactly supported initial data. We consider three cases: for $p=3$ we construct blow-up solutions in all dimensions $d\geq 9$, for $p=5$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 7$, while for $p=7$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 6$. The solutions we construct here appear to be the first blow-up solutions of defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equations with smooth real-valued data. The main step is the construction of nonzero \emph{discretely self-similar profiles} that are periodic in self-similar time and real-analytic across the light cone. We find approximate profiles by numerical continuation from rotating self-similar solutions of the complex-valued equation and upgrade them to exact solutions by a computer-assisted Newton--Kantorovich argument in a Banach algebra of Fourier--Chebyshev coefficients. The main analytic ingredients are an exact description of the linear mode operators and uniform bounds for their inverses. The codes for the computer-assisted parts of the proofs, together with the approximate solutions, are available on GitHub \cite{code}.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru D. Ionescu, Stan Palasek

item.title: Transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.20480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the fractal refinement of the Carleson's problem: (1) We introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive PDEs on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their Fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same Hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. As applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. Consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized Boussinesq and Beam propagations, while establishing new results for the both of them in higher dimensions and for Klein-Gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) Next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional Schr\"odinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. Applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. As special cases, we recover the known result for the Beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized Boussinesq and the Klein-Gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) We study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the Schr\"odinger, fractional Schr\"odinger (with convex and concave phases), Beam, linearized Boussinesq, Wave and Klein-Gordon equations. This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain quantitative results on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of \v{Z}ubrini\'c, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Utsav Dewan

item.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Deangelis

item.title: Local rigidity of conformally Euclidean metrics for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation at fixed energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.25314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove local rigidity of smooth conformally Euclidean metrics $g_0$ on smooth compact domains $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge3$, for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation $(-\Delta_g -k^2)u =0$ at a fixed energy $k^2>0$ which is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta_{g_0}$ in $M$. Any smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ in $H^s(M)$, with integer $s>n/2+1$, and having the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, is its pullback by a smooth diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. The proof uses a Helmholtz embedding to fix the gauge and a compactness argument together with a characterization of the kernel of the linearization.
item.dc:creator: Sebasti\'an Mu\~noz-Thon, Plamen Stefanov

item.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.31480v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2\epsilon$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_\epsilon$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_\epsilon$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_\epsilon$ and $b_\epsilon$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hadr\'e, Richard M. H\"ofer

item.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
item.description: arXiv:2610.32804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_\epsilon$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $\epsilon$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hadr\'e, Richard M. H\"ofer

item.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
item.dc:creator: Tahir Boudjeriou, Filippo Dell'Oro

item.title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Amp\`ere equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35192v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Amp\`ere equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally H\"older continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,\eta}$, $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Fan Cui (School of Mathematics Science, Tianjin Normal University, Tianjin, China), Huaiyu Jian (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China, Department of Mathematical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), You Li (School of Mathematics and Computational Science, Xiangtan University, Hunan, China), Yannan Liu (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China)

item.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.35266v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Lukang Sun

item.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
item.description: arXiv:2408.09238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
item.dc:creator: Illya Koval, Amir Vig

item.title: GBDT with nontrivial seeds: explicit solutions of the focusing NLS equations and the corresponding Weyl functions
item.description: arXiv:2506.07702v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our GBDT (generalised B\"acklund-Darboux transformation) approach is used to construct explicit solutions of the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in the case of the exponential seed $a \exp\{2 i (cx +dt)\}$. The corresponding Baker-Akhiezer functions and evolution of the Weyl functions are obtained as well. In particular, the solutions, which appear in the study of rogue waves, step-like solutions and $N$-modulation solutions of the NLS equation are considered. This work is an essential development of our joint work with Rien Kaashoek and Israel Gohberg, where the seed was trivial, as well as several other of our previous works.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Sakhnovich

item.title: A Li-Yau gradient estimate for the Finslerian logarithmic Schr\"{o}dinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2507.06237v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a local Li--Yau type gradient estimate for a nonlinear parabolic equation with logarithmic reaction on a forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold. The coefficients may depend on both space and time. The estimate uses a weighted Ricci curvature lower bound and explicit cutoff bounds for the divergence-form linearized Laplacian. We explain the role of this localization assumption when the reference direction varies with the solution. Applications include a local Harnack inequality for the equation with a potential and an upper bound for positive stationary solutions under a suitable cutoff exhaustion. An appendix gives a variational existence proof for positive bounded initial data, with quantitative bounds on every finite time interval, which is new as far as the authors know.
item.dc:creator: Duoxin Li, Zisu Zhao

item.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2512.16506v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Ood Shabtai

item.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
item.description: arXiv:2601.22665v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,\alpha}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(\Lambda/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
item.description: arXiv:2605.15031v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone. The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4\epsilon^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $\epsilon$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.29502v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and the borderline is determined by the K\"ahler angle.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: Topology, Morse Index, and Area of Minimal Surfaces in Three-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.32001v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, in every closed Riemannian three-manifold $(M^3,\bar g)$, there exists a constant $C=C(M,\bar g)>0$ such that every closed smoothly embedded minimal surface $\Sigma\subset M$ satisfies $b_1(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}_2)\le C\bigl(\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)+\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma)\bigr)$, establishing Song's additive genus-index-area conjecture. For closed connected orientable two-sided minimal immersions, we prove the universal inequality $\gamma(\Sigma)\le8\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive Ricci curvature and the estimate $\gamma(\Sigma)\le C(M,\bar g)\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive scalar curvature. In the latter case, we also bound both area and total curvature by $C(M,\bar g)(1+\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma))$.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Caniato

item.title: Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
item.description: arXiv:2610.25327v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) does not guarantee internal observability for a wave equation with a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable. For this same domain and observation set, we construct a smooth $2\pi$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_\Omega=L^2(\Omega)\times H^{-1}(\Omega)$ on every finite time interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane. This local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is then obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. The planar construction also yields counterexamples in every space dimension $n\ge3$. For comparison, and to identify a geometry that supplies both propagation and continuation, we show on the unit disk that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials. The proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

item.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{it\Delta}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.

item.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.35000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.
